This is my analysis. It is not possible to tile an 8x8 chessboard with 2x1 dominoes if two opposite corners are removed. Here's why:

An 8x8 chessboard has 64 squares, evenly divided into 32 black and 32 white squares. Each 2x1 domino, regardless of its orientation, always covers one black and one white square. Therefore, to completely tile the board, the number of black and white squares must be equal.

When two opposite corners are removed, both of those squares are of the same color (since opposite corners on a chessboard are always the same color). This leaves 62 squares in total, but now the count of black and white squares is unbalanced—30 of one color and 32 of the other.

Since each domino must cover one black and one white square, it is impossible to cover all 62 squares with dominoes when there is an imbalance in the number of black and white squares. Thus, tiling the board is not possible.

This is my analysis.
